drivingQuestion: Which partly emerged fetus, and which piece severed before slaughter, does the mother animal's slaughter render permitted?
outcomeNote: A mishna opening the chapter and stating the law; no question is raised, attacked or answered within this unit.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ בְּהֵמָה הַמְקַשָּׁה לֵילֵד, וְהוֹצִיא הָעוּבָּר אֶת יָדוֹ וְהֶחְזִירוֹ – מוּתָּר בַּאֲכִילָה. הוֹצִיא אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֶחְזִירוֹ – הֲרֵי זֶה כְּיָלוּד.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» When a pregnant kosher animal is slaughtered, the slaughter also renders the consumption of its fetus permitted. Even if «an animal was encountering difficulty giving birth and» meanwhile «the fetus extended its foreleg» outside the mother animal’s womb «and» then «brought it back» inside, and then the mother animal was slaughtered, the «consumption» of the fetus is «permitted» by virtue of the slaughter of the mother animal. But if the fetus «extended its head» outside the womb, «even if it» then «brought it back» inside, the halakhic status of «that» fetus is «like» that of «a newborn,» and the slaughter of the mother animal does not permit the consumption of the fetus. Rather, it requires its own slaughter.

segments.he: חוֹתֵךְ מֵעוּבָּר שֶׁבְּמֵעֶיהָ – מוּתָּר בַּאֲכִילָה, מִן הַטְּחוֹל וּמִן הַכְּלָיוֹת – אָסוּר בַּאֲכִילָה. זֶה הַכְּלָל: דָּבָר שֶׁגּוּפָהּ – אָסוּר, וְשֶׁאֵינָהּ גּוּפָהּ – מוּתָּר.
segments.en: If, prior to slaughtering an animal, one «severs» pieces «from a fetus that is in» the «womb» and leaves those pieces in the womb, their «consumption» is «permitted» by virtue of the slaughter of the mother animal. By contrast, if one severs pieces «of the spleen or of the kidneys» of an animal and then slaughters it, then even if those pieces are left inside the animal their «consumption» is «prohibited,» because an organ severed from a living being is not permitted by the subsequent slaughter of the animal. «This is the principle: An item that is» part of an animal’s «body» that was severed prior to its slaughter is «prohibited» even after slaughter, «and» an item «that is not» part of «its body,» i.e., its fetus, is «permitted» by virtue of its slaughter.

moves.summary: a fetus that extended its foreleg and brought it back is permitted by the slaughter of its mother
a fetus that extended its head, even if it brought it back, has the status of a newborn and needs its own slaughter
pieces cut from the fetus in the womb are permitted by the mother's slaughter, but pieces cut from her own spleen or kidneys are prohibited
moves.about: the mishna abstracts from its own two rulings the criterion that decides them — only what is part of the mother's own body is barred by pre-slaughter severance, while what is not part of her body (the fetus) is permitted by her slaughter

moves.summary: the mishna states the criterion governing the preceding cases: what is her body is prohibited, what is not her body is permitted
